correctness.rationale: Equality in Hölder identifies the nonempty norming face exactly with aligned unit L1 densities supported on A; splitting u into aligned mass m and its disjoint remainder gives exact distance 2(1-m), including m=0. With b_A negative-aligned mass and b_B complementary mass, 1-<g,u> >= 2b_A+(1-r)b_B while face distance is 2(b_A+b_B). Near-maximizing positive-measure subsets of B yield sharp 2/(1-r) and divergence as r->1, with B null yielding constant 1 via negative face. For the adjusted property, strong Birkhoff-James orthogonality to h in a gap case forces positive and negative sign(g)h on A, enabling an aligned face vector with h=0. In the gapless case the explicit h=sgn(g) on A, -sgn(g) on nonzero B has g perpendicular in both strong directions, yet no norming vector h-orthogonal. Checked cases A empty (nonattaining), B null, r=0, r<1, r=1. Independently tested a three-atom rational witness g=(1,-1,3/4), u supported on third atom, which gives exact ratio 8; finite tests do not replace arbitrary-measure proof.
residual_risks: Norming face/error K undefined when A null; only real scalars and positive face.
The proof, not finite rational 14,772 tests asserted by packaged checker, handles nonatomic or unbounded-atom count spaces.

value.rationale: This gives a complete real L1 structural classification across arbitrary probability measures, including gapless failure, and a sharp measure-free quantitative norming-face stability profile. The optimal constant diverges precisely at the classification boundary, making it useful for perturbation and approximation of norming vectors rather than routine manipulation of Hölder equality.
residual_risks: Only scalar real functionals and positive norming face; cannot extrapolate to operator-valued/complex Bhatia–Šemrl.

final_claim: For real norm-one g in L_infinity over any probability space, adjusted Bhatia-Semrl holds iff the maximum-modulus set A has positive measure and either B is null or esssup_B|g|<1; the exact face-distance formula holds, with optimal error constant 1 when B null, 2/(1-r) when r<1, and infinity for gapless non-null B.
limitations: Face-distance only when norm-attainment set A nonnull; g norm one, probability measure arbitrary.
Possible hidden implication from norm exposure/stability theory; finite atom checks are supplementary.
